exercises.english: I have the book.
exercises.why: Buch is neuter, and das does not change in the Akkusativ.

exercises.english: He is eating the apple.
exercises.why: Apfel is masculine and the direct object of isst, so der becomes den.

exercises.english: She is looking for the key.
exercises.why: Schlüssel is masculine and the direct object of sucht, so der becomes den.

exercises.english: Do you know the way?
exercises.why: Weg is masculine and the direct object of kennst, so der becomes den.

exercises.english: I need the computer.
exercises.why: Computer is masculine and the direct object of brauche, so der becomes den.

exercises.english: They see the friends.
exercises.why: Freunde is plural, and die does not change in the Akkusativ.

exercises.english: Do you hear the music?
exercises.why: Musik is feminine, and die does not change in the Akkusativ.

exercises.english: I am cooking the potatoes.
exercises.why: Kartoffeln is plural, and die does not change in the Akkusativ.

exercises.english: He is drinking the juice.
exercises.why: Saft is masculine and the direct object of trinkt, so der becomes den.

exercises.english: I would like the picture.
exercises.why: Bild is neuter, and das does not change in the Akkusativ.

exercises.english: I am looking for my phone.
exercises.why: Handy is neuter, so mein takes no ending in the Akkusativ.

exercises.english: I am asking my friend.
exercises.why: Freundin is feminine, so mein takes -e: meine.

exercises.english: I love my child.
exercises.why: Kind is neuter, so mein takes no ending in the Akkusativ.

exercises.english: I am visiting my parents.
exercises.why: Eltern is plural, so mein takes -e: meine.

exercises.english: I am eating my bread roll.
exercises.why: Semmel is feminine, so mein takes -e: meine.

exercises.english: I am drinking my coffee.
exercises.why: Kaffee is masculine and the direct object, so mein takes -en: meinen.

exercises.english: I forget my appointment at the doctor's.
exercises.why: Termin is masculine and the direct object, so mein takes -en: meinen.

exercises.english: I am listening to my favorite band.
exercises.why: Band is feminine, so mein takes -e: meine.

exercises.english: I open my eyes.
exercises.why: Augen is plural, so mein takes -e: meine.

exercises.english: He doesn't have a car.
exercises.why: Auto is neuter, so kein takes no ending in the Akkusativ.

exercises.english: We don't need any help.
exercises.why: Hilfe is feminine, so kein takes -e: keine.

exercises.english: I'm giving my brother a football.
exercises.why: Bruder is masculine and the one receiving, so mein takes -em: meinem.

exercises.english: I'm giving my sister a book.
exercises.why: Schwester is feminine and the one receiving, so mein takes -er: meiner.

exercises.english: I'm giving my child a present.
exercises.why: Kind is neuter, and neuter takes the same Dativ ending as masculine: meinem.

exercises.english: I'm giving my parents a trip.
exercises.why: Eltern is plural, and the Dativ plural takes -en: meinen.

exercises.english: I'm showing my friend the photo.
exercises.why: Freund is masculine and the one receiving, so mein takes -em: meinem.

exercises.english: I'm bringing my mother flowers.
exercises.why: Mutter is feminine and the one receiving, so mein takes -er: meiner.

exercises.english: I'm helping my brother.
exercises.why: helfen always takes the Dativ, and Bruder is masculine: meinem.

exercises.english: I'm helping my grandparents.
exercises.why: helfen always takes the Dativ, and the Dativ plural takes -en: meinen.

categories.title: Dativ: Personal Pronouns
categories.subtitle: mir / dir / ihm / ihr / uns / euch / ihnen / Ihnen
categories.ruleNote: Dativ: mir (ich), dir (du), ihm (er/es), ihr (sie), uns (wir), euch (ihr), ihnen (sie pl.), Ihnen (Sie)

exercises.english: Tomorrow I'm buying myself a bike!
exercises.why: the bike is for me, and ich becomes mir in the Dativ.

exercises.sentence: Schreibst du ______ eine Karte aus dem Urlaub?
exercises.english: Will you write me a postcard from your vacation?
exercises.why: the card is written to me, and ich becomes mir in the Dativ.

exercises.english: I'll write you a postcard too.
exercises.why: the card goes to you, and du becomes dir in the Dativ.

exercises.english: Does the car belong to you all?
exercises.why: gehören always takes the Dativ, and ihr becomes euch.

exercises.english: They like that a lot.
exercises.why: gefallen always takes the Dativ, and plural sie becomes ihnen.

exercises.english: Dad, did you bring us something?
exercises.why: the something is for us, and wir becomes uns in the Dativ.

exercises.english: Then I'll bake her a cake.
exercises.why: the cake is for her, and sie becomes ihr in the Dativ.

exercises.english: Can you lend him something?
exercises.why: the lending goes to him, and er becomes ihm in the Dativ.

exercises.english: Mr Schmitt, does this bag belong to you?
exercises.why: gehören takes the Dativ, and formal Sie becomes Ihnen, still capitalized.

categories.title: Two-Way Prepositions: Wohin or Wo?
categories.subtitle: Movement takes the Akkusativ, location the Dativ
categories.ruleNote: Wohin? (movement) takes the Akkusativ · Wo? (location) takes the Dativ

exercises.sentence: Ich hänge das Bild an ______ Wand.
exercises.english: I'm hanging the picture on the wall.
exercises.why: the picture is being moved there, so an answers Wohin? and takes the Akkusativ: die Wand.

exercises.english: The picture is hanging on the wall.
exercises.why: the picture is already there, so an answers Wo? and takes the Dativ: der Wand.

exercises.sentence: Ich lege das Buch auf ______ Tisch.
exercises.english: I'm putting the book on the table.
exercises.why: legen moves the book somewhere, so auf answers Wohin? and takes the Akkusativ: den Tisch.

exercises.english: The book is lying on the table.
exercises.why: liegen is a position, so auf answers Wo? and takes the Dativ: dem Tisch.

exercises.english: We're going to the cinema today.
exercises.why: gehen is movement into it, so in answers Wohin? and takes the Akkusativ: das Kino.

exercises.english: We're already sitting in the cinema.
exercises.why: sitzen is a position, so in answers Wo? and takes the Dativ: dem Kino.

exercises.english: The cat runs under the bed.
exercises.why: the cat is moving under it, so unter answers Wohin? and takes the Akkusativ: das Bett.

exercises.english: The cat is sleeping under the bed.
exercises.why: schlafen happens in one place, so unter answers Wo? and takes the Dativ: dem Bett.

exercises.english: Put the chair next to the sofa.
exercises.why: stellen puts it somewhere, so neben answers Wohin? and takes the Akkusativ: das Sofa.

exercises.english: The chair is standing next to the sofa.
exercises.why: stehen is a position, so neben answers Wo? and takes the Dativ: dem Sofa.

exercises.sentence: Ich fahre das Auto vor ______ Garage.
exercises.english: I'm driving the car in front of the garage.
exercises.why: the car ends up there, so vor answers Wohin? and takes the Akkusativ: die Garage.

exercises.english: The car is parked in front of the garage.
exercises.why: the car is already there, so vor answers Wo? and takes the Dativ: der Garage.

categories.title: Prepositions: Which Case?
categories.subtitle: The preposition decides the case
categories.ruleNote: Akkusativ after durch, für, ohne, um · Dativ after aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu · Genitiv after trotz, während, wegen

exercises.sentence: Ich fahre mit ______ Bus zur Arbeit.
exercises.english: I take the bus to work.
exercises.why: mit always takes the Dativ, and Bus is masculine: dem Bus.

exercises.english: The present is for the teacher.
exercises.why: für always takes the Akkusativ, and Lehrer is masculine: den Lehrer.

exercises.english: We're walking through the park.
exercises.why: durch always takes the Akkusativ, and Park is masculine: den Park.

exercises.english: She comes from Switzerland.
exercises.why: aus always takes the Dativ, and Schweiz is feminine: der Schweiz.

exercises.english: After dinner we go for a walk.
exercises.why: nach always takes the Dativ, and Essen is neuter: dem Essen.

exercises.english: I'm going for a walk without the dog.
exercises.why: ohne always takes the Akkusativ, and Hund is masculine: den Hund.

exercises.english: We're sitting around the table.
exercises.why: um always takes the Akkusativ, and Tisch is masculine: den Tisch.

exercises.english: I live at my parents' place.
exercises.why: bei always takes the Dativ, and the Dativ plural is den.

exercises.english: I've been learning German for a week.
exercises.why: seit always takes the Dativ, and Woche is feminine: einer Woche.

exercises.sentence: Das ist ein Geschenk von ______ Schwester.
exercises.english: That's a present from my sister.
exercises.why: von always takes the Dativ, and Schwester is feminine: meiner Schwester.

exercises.english: Despite the rain we're going for a walk.
exercises.why: trotz takes the Genitiv, and masculine nouns take des plus an -s: des Regens.

exercises.sentence: Wegen ______ Wetters bleiben wir zu Hause.
exercises.english: Because of the weather we're staying home.
exercises.why: wegen takes the Genitiv, and neuter nouns take des plus an -s: des Wetters.

categories.title: Which Preposition?
categories.subtitle: The case after the blank gives it away
categories.ruleNote: The article after the blank shows the case, and the case tells you which preposition fits.

exercises.sentence: Ich fahre ______ dem Bus zur Arbeit.
exercises.english: I take the bus to work.
exercises.why: dem is Dativ, and going by a vehicle takes mit.

exercises.english: The present is for my brother.
exercises.why: meinen is Akkusativ, and something intended for someone takes für.

exercises.english: She comes from Switzerland.
exercises.why: der is Dativ here, and coming out of a country takes aus.

exercises.english: We're walking through the park.
exercises.why: den is Akkusativ, and moving from one side to the other takes durch.

exercises.english: After dinner we go for a walk.
exercises.why: dem is Dativ, and 'after' in time takes nach.

exercises.english: I've been learning German for a year.
exercises.why: einem is Dativ, and a stretch of time still going on takes seit.

exercises.sentence: Ich gehe ______ meinen Bruder ins Kino.
exercises.english: I'm going to the cinema without my brother.
exercises.why: meinen is Akkusativ, and leaving someone out takes ohne.

exercises.english: We're sitting around the table.
exercises.why: den is Akkusativ, and sitting around something takes um.

exercises.english: I'm flying to Italy tomorrow.
exercises.why: countries and cities used without an article take nach for the destination.

exercises.sentence: ______ des schlechten Wetters bleiben wir zu Hause.
exercises.english: Because of the bad weather we're staying home.
exercises.why: des is Genitiv, and giving the reason takes wegen.

exercises.english: Everyone is here except my brother.
exercises.why: meinem is Dativ, and leaving one person out of a group takes außer.

exercises.sentence: Das ist ein Geschenk ______ meiner Schwester.
exercises.english: That's a present from my sister.
exercises.why: meiner is Dativ, and the giver or the origin takes von.

categories.title: Short Forms: ins, im, zum, zur
categories.subtitle: Preposition and article contracted
categories.ruleNote: in + das = ins · in + dem = im · zu + dem = zum · zu + der = zur · an + das = ans · an + dem = am

exercises.english: We're going to the cinema this evening.
exercises.why: movement into it takes in plus Akkusativ, and in + das contracts to ins.

exercises.english: We were at the cinema yesterday.
exercises.why: being somewhere takes in plus Dativ, and in + dem contracts to im.

exercises.english: I'm going to the doctor tomorrow.
exercises.why: zu always takes the Dativ, and zu + dem contracts to zum.

exercises.english: My daughter already goes to school.
exercises.why: Schule is feminine, and zu + der contracts to zur.

exercises.sentence: Er geht ______ Fenster und schaut hinaus.
exercises.english: He goes to the window and looks out.
exercises.why: gehen is movement, so an takes the Akkusativ, and an + das contracts to ans.

exercises.sentence: Er steht ______ Fenster und schaut hinaus.
exercises.english: He is standing at the window looking out.
exercises.why: stehen is a position, so an takes the Dativ, and an + dem contracts to am.

exercises.english: I've just come from the baker's.
exercises.why: von always takes the Dativ, and von + dem contracts to vom.

exercises.english: I ran into her at the baker's.
exercises.why: bei always takes the Dativ, and bei + dem contracts to beim.

exercises.english: I'm already looking forward to the weekend.
exercises.why: sich freuen auf takes the Akkusativ, and auf + das contracts to aufs.

exercises.english: On Sunday I sleep in.
exercises.why: days take an plus Dativ, and an + dem contracts to am.

exercises.english: In summer we go to the sea.
exercises.why: seasons take in plus Dativ, and in + dem contracts to im.

exercises.english: The ball rolls under the car.
exercises.why: rollen is movement, so unter takes the Akkusativ, and unter + das contracts to unters.
